exposure: years of overall registered nursing experience
outcome: individual cesarean rates for women with low-risk pregnancies (NTSV)
cohort: The study participants were 68 labor and delivery nurses, and their individual cesarean rates were calculated from retrospective chart reviews of women with low-risk pregnancies (nulliparous, term, singleton, vertex; NTSV) whose births they attended.
finding: Nurses with more years of work experience and those working day shifts, as charge nurses, or part-time/per-diem had greater odds of lower cesarean rates for women with low-risk pregnancies.
mod_finding: Increased nursing experience and specific work characteristics (day shift, charge nurse, part-time/per-diem) were associated with lower individual cesarean delivery rates for women with low-risk pregnancies.
cross-section timing: One-time online survey; retrospective chart reviews for C-section rates
